claims.text: Overall Green Flood in Afghanistan from 19 Jul 2026 01:00 UTC to 21 Jul 2026 01:00 UTC. Flood can have a low humanitarian impact based on the magnitude, exposed population and vulnerability. At least 20 people were killed, around 80 others injured, and more than 100 remain missing, in Nuristan Province following flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall.

Re-checked 8 August 2026: WHO's Situation Report No. 3 (3 August 2026) remains the final report in that series and OCHA's Flash Update #3 (28 July 2026) remains the latest Flash Update; no Flash Update #4 or newer WHO report has been published, and the combined confirmed toll (at least 30 deaths) is unchanged.

Re-checked 9 August 2026: OCHA Flash Update #3 (28 July 2026) remains the latest in its series; no Flash Update #4 has been published, and the combined confirmed death toll (at least 30 across eastern Afghanistan) is unchanged.

Re-checked 10 August 2026: the ReliefWeb disaster page's Latest Updates list shows an IFRC DREF Operation report (MDRAF022, posted 6 August 2026) as the newest item; no OCHA Flash Update #4 or newer WHO situation report has been published. The IFRC report documents damage specifically in Parun City (30 houses damaged, of which 7 destroyed; destruction of a mosque, the municipality building, and seven markets; roughly 45 livestock lost) without providing an updated aggregate death toll. The combined confirmed toll (at least 30 deaths) is unchanged.

Re-checked 11 August 2026: direct fetch of ReliefWeb's Afghanistan flooding disaster page and individual report pages returned HTTP 403 today; GDACS's event report for FL 1104033 (re-fetched) still shows the Green flood alert for 19-21 July 2026 with no newer episode published. A targeted web search found no OCHA Flash Update #4, no WHO situation report newer than No. 3 (3 August 2026), and no ReliefWeb item newer than the IFRC DREF report (6 August 2026) already on file. The combined confirmed toll (at least 30 deaths) remains unchanged.

UN News (22 July 2026): flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall on 20 July have killed at least 26 people across eastern Afghanistan, including 23 in Nuristan province, where homes, markets and roads were swept away, with the worst devastation in Parun City (7 houses completely destroyed, 23 partially damaged, 70 shops and 11 hotels damaged, 40 vehicles lost). The floods also killed three Afghan refugees at a returnee transit camp near the Torkham border crossing with Pakistan and injured nine others there. OCHA said the immediate priority is to save lives and reach people who may still be missing or injured, and warned that casualty figures could rise as more information becomes available; UNICEF and partners are setting up a field clinic in Parun for trauma care.

OCHA Flash Update #2: Flooding in Eastern Afghanistan (22-23 July 2026): in Parun City, Nuristan Province, local authorities report 23 killed, 5 missing (down from over 100) and 125 injured (38 severe, 87 minor). At the Torkham transit camp in Nangarhar, 3 Afghan refugees were killed and 9 injured (unchanged). One additional death is reported in Maidan Wardak province (Sayedabad District). The response has moved from immediate search and rescue and emergency life-saving assistance towards a broader, multi-sector response addressing shelter, health, food, WASH, protection, livelihoods and planning to address early recovery needs.

OCHA Flash Update #3: Flooding in Central, Eastern and Southeastern Afghanistan (as of 28 July 2026): in Laghman Province, three people were killed and four others injured, with 187 families affected and 183 houses damaged or destroyed; approximately 800 acres of seasonal crops and around 310 livestock were also reportedly lost or damaged. Nuristan Province remains the most severely affected area; the completed inter-agency needs assessment in Parun district identified 120 families eligible for humanitarian assistance, of which the first 92 have already received assistance. The Shelter/NFI cluster reports 1,168 families have been affected across 14 provinces, including 234 houses completely destroyed and 930 houses damaged. Needs assessments in Maidan Wardak and Panjshir are expected to commence shortly.

Re-checked 1 August 2026: OCHA's Flash Update #3 (data as of 28 July 2026, posted 29 July) remains the latest report in the Afghanistan flooding series on ReliefWeb; no Flash Update #4 has been published, and figures are unchanged from the prior check.
Re-checked 2 August 2026: OCHA Flash Update #3 (28 July 2026) remains the latest in the series; no Flash Update #4 has been published as of 2 August 2026, and figures are unchanged.

Re-checked 5 August 2026: OCHA Flash Update #3 (28 July 2026) remains the latest report in the Afghanistan flooding series; a targeted search found no Flash Update #4 published as of 5 August 2026, and figures (30 combined confirmed deaths, 1,168 families affected across 14 provinces) are unchanged.

Re-confirmed by direct fetch on 6 August 2026: OCHA's Afghanistan Flash Update #3 (28 July 2026, published 29 July, modified 30 July) remains the latest in its series; no Flash Update #4 has been published. Confirmed unchanged: Laghman 'three people were killed and four others were injured, with 187 families affected'; Shelter/NFI cluster '1,168 families have been affected across 14 provinces, including 234 houses completely destroyed and 930 houses damaged.'

WHO's Situation Report No. 3 on the flash floods in Afghanistan (published 3 August 2026 on ReliefWeb, data as of 15:00 on 30 July 2026, described by WHO as its final situation report on this response) records cumulative Key Figures of 29 fatalities, 129 injuries and 4 missing, broken down as 26 deaths in the Eastern region (23 Nuristan, 3 Laghman), 1 death in the Central region, and further deaths in Paktika's Barmal district and Paktia province in the Southeastern region. This WHO cumulative figure reflects domestic flood-affected provinces only and does not include the 3 Afghan refugees killed at the Torkham border transit camp that OCHA's Flash Update series counted toward the combined 30-death toll already on file; the two figures use different scopes and neither supersedes the other.

description: Torrential monsoon rains triggered flash floods in Afghanistan's eastern Nuristan province beginning around 19 July 2026, striking the provincial capital Parun and surrounding villages, and also killed Afghan refugees at a returnee transit camp near the Torkham border crossing. GDACS assessed the event as an overall Green alert for low humanitarian impact. OCHA's Flash Update #2 (23 July 2026) reported the confirmed death toll had held near 27 across eastern Afghanistan while the number of people missing in Nuristan had fallen sharply from over 100 to 5. OCHA's Flash Update #3 (as of 28 July 2026) shows the response has now broadened geographically to Central, Eastern and Southeastern Afghanistan, with new flood-related casualties confirmed in Laghman Province (3 killed, 4 injured, 187 families affected) in addition to the original Nuristan/Torkham/Maidan Wardak toll. Nuristan remains the most severely affected area, where a completed inter-agency needs assessment in Parun district identified 120 families eligible for assistance. No newer OCHA Flash Update has been published as of 5 August 2026, and figures remain unchanged. Re-checked 9 August 2026: OCHA Flash Update #3 (28 July 2026) remains the latest in its series; no Flash Update #4 has been published, and the combined confirmed death toll (at least 30 across eastern Afghanistan) is unchanged. Re-checked 10 August 2026: an IFRC DREF Operation report (6 August 2026) is the newest item on ReliefWeb's disaster page but provides no updated aggregate death toll; the combined confirmed toll (at least 30 deaths) remains unchanged. Re-checked 11 August 2026: direct fetch of ReliefWeb's Afghanistan flooding disaster page and report pages returned HTTP 403 today, but GDACS's event report for FL 1104033 (re-fetched) still shows the Green flood alert for 19-21 July 2026 with no newer episode, and a targeted web search found no OCHA Flash Update #4, no WHO situation report newer than No. 3, and no ReliefWeb item newer than the IFRC DREF report (6 August 2026) already on file. The combined confirmed toll (at least 30 deaths) remains the freshest available figure and is unchanged.

impact.summary: OCHA's Flash Update #2 (23 July 2026) reported 23 people killed and 5 still missing (down from 100+) in Nuristan Province, with 125 injured (38 severe, 87 minor) there; the 3 Afghan refugees killed and 9 injured at the Torkham border transit camp and 1 additional death in Maidan Wardak province were unchanged — a combined toll of 27 confirmed deaths across eastern Afghanistan. OCHA's Flash Update #3 (as of 28 July 2026) broadens the response to Central, Eastern and Southeastern Afghanistan and reports 3 further deaths and 4 injuries in Laghman Province (187 families affected, 183 houses damaged/destroyed), bringing the combined confirmed death toll to at least 30. Nuristan remains the most severely affected area, with a completed inter-agency needs assessment in Parun district identifying 120 families eligible for assistance (92 already assisted); the Shelter/NFI cluster now reports 1,168 families affected across 14 provinces (234 houses destroyed, 930 damaged). No authoritative source has declared the event resolved.
